items.followUp: What information should you identify when analysing a problem?

rubric.why: Understanding begins with identifying the problem’s purpose or requirement.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that the problem statement must be analysed to determine its purpose or requirement.

rubric.why: Identifying the input and expected output clarifies what the problem needs.
rubric.description: Identify the input and expected output.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the required input and output should be identified.

modelAnswer: Read and analyse the problem statement to understand what it requires.
Identify the input data and the expected output.

items.followUp: Draw the flowchart symbols for Start/Stop and Decision.

rubric.why: A rectangle is the standard flowchart symbol for a processing step.
rubric.description: Draw and label the Processing symbol as a rectangle.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correctly drawn and labelled rectangle.

rubric.why: A parallelogram is the standard flowchart symbol for input and output.
rubric.description: Draw and label the Input/Output symbol as a parallelogram.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correctly drawn and labelled parallelogram.

items.followUp: Write two advantages of using a flowchart.

rubric.why: Preparing a flowchart can take considerable time.
rubric.description: State that flowcharts take time to prepare.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the time required to draw a flowchart as a disadvantage.

rubric.why: Changes to a flowchart may require redrawing parts or all of it, especially when it is complex.
rubric.description: State that flowcharts are difficult to modify or become difficult to manage for complex problems.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for either valid disadvantage.

modelAnswer: Flowcharts take a considerable amount of time to draw.
They are difficult to modify, especially when they are large or complex.

items.followUp: List the main sections of a webpage.

rubric.why: The header and navigation are common main sections of a webpage.
rubric.description: List the header and navigation bar.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for listing both the header and navigation bar.

rubric.why: The main content and footer are common webpage sections; a sidebar may also be included.
rubric.description: List the main content and footer, with a sidebar as an acceptable additional section.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for listing the main content and footer, or the content, sidebar and footer.

items.followUp: What happens to the contents of volatile memory when the power is switched off?

rubric.description: Identify volatile memory as temporary memory.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing volatile memory as temporary memory.

rubric.why: Volatile memory requires power to retain its contents.
rubric.description: State that its contents are lost when power is switched off.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly stating that data is lost when power is removed.

modelAnswer: Volatile memory is temporary memory that requires a continuous power supply.
Its contents are lost when the power is switched off.

items.followUp: When does an AND operator give a true result?

rubric.why: AND is a logical operator used with Boolean conditions.
rubric.description: Identify AND as a logical or Boolean operator.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly identifying the type of operator.

rubric.why: The AND operation is true only when both operands or conditions are true.
rubric.description: State the condition for an AND result to be true.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that both conditions must be true.

modelAnswer: It gives a true result only when both conditions are true.

rubric.why: The decimal number is expressed as a sum of powers of 2.
rubric.description: Show the correct place-value decomposition of 156.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying 156 as 128 + 16 + 8 + 4, or equivalent correct working.

rubric.why: The place values from 128 to 1 produce the binary digits 10011100.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct final binary answer.

modelAnswer: Reading the coefficients of 128, 64, 32, 16, 8, 4, 2 and 1 gives 1 0 0 1 1 1 0 0.

items.followUp: What protection does a patent give to an inventor?

rubric.why: A patent grants the inventor a legal exclusive right over the invention.
rubric.description: Explain that a patent gives an inventor a legal or exclusive right.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a patent grants a legal or exclusive right.

rubric.why: Patent protection restricts others from exploiting the invention without the inventor’s permission.
rubric.description: State that it prevents others from making, using or selling the invention without permission.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the restriction on unauthorised use or exploitation of the invention.

modelAnswer: A patent is a legal right granted to an inventor for an invention.
It gives the inventor exclusive protection and prevents others from making, using or selling the invention without permission.
